## Overview

- **Project:** Comparing ARIMA and Random Forest for stress state 
detection using WESAD wearable sensor data
- **Goal:** Determine if ARIMA can match Random Forest in classifying 
stress states without complex training
- **Approach:** Extract ECG and EDA signals, engineer rolling window 
features, evaluate with F1-score and confusion matrix

## What is Random Forest {.smaller}

- Random Forest is an ensemble machine learning method that builds multiple decision trees
- Makes no assumptions about linearity or distribution of the underlying data
- Classification is determined by majority vote across B trees:

$$\hat{m}(x) = \text{mode}\{T_1(x), T_2(x), \ldots, T_B(x)\}$$

## Why Random Forest for Stress Detection on WESAD {.smaller}

- **Proven on WESAD** — Garg et al. (2021) found RF achieved strong performance across binary and three-class stress tasks; Schmidt et al. (2018) achieved 88.33% baseline accuracy
- **Handles non-linear patterns** — stress responses in ECG and EDA are non-linear; RF captures complex patterns without linearity assumptions [@ziyadidegan2025]
- **Robust to sensor noise** — RF node-splitting prevents outliers from corrupting classification boundaries [@garg2021]
